newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-SWINBURN ON IRISH CHARITY WALK AFTER ACCIDENT.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SWINBURN ON IRISH CHARITY WALK AFTER ACCIDENT.

text.p: Jockey Walter Swinburn, almost killed in a horrific riding accident in Hong Kong last year, is to walk across Ireland to raise funds for charity.
"I received a lot of support on my way back and it's important for me to give something back," he told the London Independent.

Swinburn, who shot to stardom when he won the Epsom Derby aboard Shergar in 1981 when he was just 19, was fortunate to escape with his life when Liffey River crashed through the rails at Hong Kong's Sha Tin course last February.

Swinburn, whose return to the saddle was sealed with an emotional Breeders Turf victory on Pilsudski in November, begins his walk from Cork to Dublin next Monday. The money raised will be divided between a Dubin hospital, an English hospice and a Hong Kong fund for young burn victims.
